control_protocol.interface: 2A simulation CSR; not an AXI-Lite pin-level contract
control_protocol.handshake: single outstanding transfer accepted on rising edge when csr_valid && csr_ready; csr_rdata is the read value on that same cycle
control_protocol.ready: csr_ready is high outside hard reset; software must change/deassert valid after each accepted transfer
control_protocol.locked_write: configuration writes are ignored unless PS owns buffers and busy/done/error are all clear
control_protocol.start: accepted only from idle after argument validation; busy=1 and PL buffer ownership begin on acceptance edge
control_protocol.status: done and error are mutually exclusive sticky bits; each remains set until its ACK bit or reset
control_protocol.register_alignment: csr_addr must be 32-bit aligned; unaligned/reserved reads return zero and writes are ignored; writes to RO registers are ignored
control_protocol.soft_reset: accepted CMD.soft_reset aborts current task and has priority over CMD.start in the same write
control_protocol.timeout: timeout_cycles must be nonzero; count rising edges after the accepted start edge; completion at the Nth edge wins over timeout, otherwise abort at that edge

operator_completion_event.direction: internal PL compute backend to PL CSR control FSM; not a PS-facing pin or CSR register
operator_completion_event.handshake: operator_result_valid is a one-cycle pulse sampled on a rising edge while busy; no backpressure; operator_error_code is stable on that edge
operator_completion_event.success: error_code=0 means all required feature/head writes completed and the result may be committed as done
operator_completion_event.error: known nonzero CSR error codes 1..7 are latched and abort the task; unknown nonzero values map to INTERNAL; error invalidates heads and returns buffer ownership to PS
operator_completion_event.timeout_boundary: a valid operator result on the Nth timeout edge wins over timeout; code 0 completes successfully and a nonzero code completes with error

control_protocol.ownership: PL owns input/weight read and feature write access while busy; ownership returns to PS on done/error/reset

memory_protocol.handshake: single outstanding word request; accepted when mem_valid && mem_ready; selected read lanes, mem_rdata and mem_error_code are valid on that same cycle
memory_protocol.alignment: 32-bit byte address; mem_addr[1:0] must be zero or the accepted request returns error code BAD_RANGE; little-endian byte lanes
memory_protocol.stability: hold valid, address, direction, write data and both strobes stable until handshake or abort
memory_protocol.access: while busy, PL may read input, weights and feature tensors; PL may write feature tensors; input and weights are read-only to PL
memory_protocol.idle_reset: testbench memory model drives mem_ready low and mem_error_code=NONE while idle or reset; while PL is busy and owns buffers, it drives mem_ready according to the frozen stall schedule; a transfer requires mem_valid && mem_ready
memory_protocol.read_strobe: read requires mem_rstrb != 0 and mem_wstrb == 0; selected lanes must each lie in one logical readable object; disabled lanes return zero
memory_protocol.write_strobe: write requires mem_wstrb != 0 and mem_rstrb == 0; selected lanes must each lie in one logical feature tensor; disabled lanes have no side effect
memory_protocol.last_word: partial read/write is required at an odd tensor tail; for a 5070-byte head the last aligned word uses lane mask 0011

error_response_codes.2: BAD_RANGE; unaligned address, selected byte outside one allowed logical object/tensor, or write to input/weights

memory_protocol.error_code_mapping: memory model returns one 3-bit project error code with the handshake; PL copies codes 1, 2 or 6 to CSR ERROR_CODE and aborts; any other nonzero response is converted to INTERNAL; failed requests have no memory side effect
memory_protocol.range_error: bad/zero/conflicting strobe returns BAD_ARGUMENT; selected bytes outside an allowed half-open logical object/tensor range or a write to input/weights returns BAD_RANGE; accepted errors abort
memory_protocol.reset_abort: hard/soft reset or timeout cancels a pending request without a later memory side effect
memory_protocol.hardware_scope: simulation-only logical memory contract; physical AXI, DMA and cache binding is deferred to approved 2B G0

operator_test_plan.scope: each supported cfg operator layer plus the shared signed INT8 MAC primitive
operator_test_plan.case_order: operator name ASCII order including int8_mac; cfg layer_index ascending within each cfg operator, random case_index 0..999 then directed case_index 0..15; int8_mac is one shared instance; directed cases consume no PRNG state
operator_test_plan.model_layer_geometry: all per-layer vectors use the exact input/output shapes, kernel, stride, padding, activation, scales and channel counts in layers; no reduced geometry or synthetic parameter override is allowed
operator_test_plan.prng: one shared xorshift32 stream; state starts 20260922; per draw apply x=(x^(x<<13))&0xffffffff, x=x^(x>>17), x=(x^(x<<5))&0xffffffff; each selector uses next_u32 % bound; each INT8 operand uses (next_u32 & 255) % 255 - 127; signed INT32 bias is next_u32 interpreted two's complement
operator_test_plan.tensor_order: NCHW contiguous; convolution reduction and maxpool window order are input_channel then kernel_y then kernel_x; route inputs follow cfg reference order then channel; spatial coordinate is row-major
operator_test_plan.int8_mac: one shared dot-product primitive; 1000 cases total with K=conv_reduction_lengths[case_index % 21], where lengths are ordered by ascending cfg layer_index; consume K activation INT8 values, K weight INT8 values, then one signed INT32 bias; exact INT64 audit precedes checked signed INT32 accumulation
operator_test_plan.convolutional: 1000 cases per cfg convolution layer; one output element per case; consume output_channel,row,col selectors then exactly K activation bytes in input_channel,kernel_y,kernel_x order, including taps later replaced by zero padding; use that layer's frozen GF8 weights, quantized bias and configured activation only; out-of-input taps contribute the layer padding value 0
operator_test_plan.maxpool: 1000 cases per cfg maxpool layer; one output element per case; consume channel,row,col selectors then exactly kernel_h*kernel_w candidate values in kernel_y,kernel_x order; replace out-of-input candidates with -127; use the layer's frozen Darknet formula/origin and actual logical shape
operator_test_plan.route: 1000 cases per cfg route layer; one spatial coordinate per case; consume y,x selectors, then source values in cfg reference order and channel order at that coordinate; requantize each source to max(input_scales) with half-away rounding and symmetric saturation before concatenation
operator_test_plan.upsample: 1000 cases per cfg upsample layer; consume output_channel,y,x selectors and the one selected source INT8 value; expected coordinate is source[channel,floor(y/stride),floor(x/stride)]
operator_test_plan.yolo: 1000 address-view queries per cfg YOLO layer; consume anchor_local,entry,row,col selectors in that order and verify byte address aliases source convolution NCHW offset
operator_test_plan.selectors_and_values: each bounded selector consumes one next_u32 and uses modulo bound; each random INT8 value consumes one next_u32 and maps (value&255)%255-127; one shared stream carries between cases and layers; no implicit reseed

directed_vector_rules.count_semantics: each case_index 0..15 is exactly one vector; directed_case_vectors is the normative materialized plan for every operator and shared int8_mac
directed_vector_rules.convolution_materialization: expanded vectors contain target_output_nchw, exact K activation bytes, the output channel's exact GFINT8W1 weight bytes in input_channel/kernel_y/kernel_x order, quantized INT32 bias, input/weight/output scales, activation and padding; source input outside this receptive field is zero; initialize accumulation from bias, add products in listed order and check signed INT32 after each addition
directed_vector_rules.int8_mac_materialization: expanded vectors contain exact K, activation/weight arrays, bias, exact INT64 sum, first signed INT32 overflow product index and expected result; short patterns repeat from element zero to exactly K
directed_vector_rules.maxpool: one kernel_h*kernel_w candidate window in kernel_y/kernel_x order; out-of-input candidates are -127; case-specific channel/row/column uses first=0,last=dimension-1,middle=floor(dimension/2)
directed_vector_rules.route_materialization: expanded route vectors select source_channel_ranges before requantization; for groups>1 Darknet selects [group_id*C/groups:(group_id+1)*C/groups] from the single source tensor; source tensors remain in cfg reference order and selected channels remain ascending; each vector records selected indices, exact source bytes, per-source requantized bytes and concatenated output bytes
directed_vector_rules.route_scale_fallback: case 9 selects the first cfg source whose scale differs from target=max(source_scales), fills only that source's selected channels with -127 and requires the requantized values to change; all other sources are zero; if all source scales equal target it uses the exact alternating [-1,1] identity-path vector and records equal_source_scales_identity
directed_vector_rules.upsample: each query has exact target output and source coordinates, selected source INT8 value, expected output, pair queries, source-tensor fill rule and zero default; alternating source profile uses flat NCHW even index=-127, odd index=+127
directed_vector_rules.yolo: one query is (anchor_local,entry,row,column); first=0,last=dimension-1,middle=floor(dimension/2); channel=anchor_local*10+entry and source address is base+(channel*height+row)*width+column
